sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of February, 2025 The Respondent No.3 in O.P.(M.V.) No.249/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ottapalam is the appellant herein.
Petitioner in the OP MV is the Cross Objector.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 17.11.2011.

According to the petitioner, on 17.11.2011 at about 8.45 a.m., while he was riding pillion on a motor cycle, a bus bearing registration No.KL 8Q 8199 driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the motor cycle and as a result of which, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the bus.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.15,00,000/-
MACA. No.2173/2015 & CO.22/2021 2025:KER:11455 4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A19, and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,33,600/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the Respondent No. 3 preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri.Mathew Jacob Senior Standing the learned Counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent/appellant, and Sri.P.V. Chandramohan, the learned Counsel for the petitioner/cross objector.
10.

The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the MACA. No.2173/2015 &
CO.22/2021 2025:KER:11455 offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was doing business, earning Rs. 3,500/- per month.
The Tribunal also fixed his monthly income at Rs.3500/-.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that as Haridasan vs The Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135743133/
3 per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2011 will come to Rs.8,000/-.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is argued that the Tribunal was not justified in fixing the notional income of the petitioner below that of a Coolie.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. It is true that as per the decision in Ramachandrappa (supra), the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2011 will come to Rs.8,000/-.
In the above circumstances, in order to award just and reasonable compensation to the petitioner, his notional income is to be fixed at least as that of a coolie.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.8,000/-.

MACA. No.2173/2015 & CO.22/2021 2025:KER:11455 12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Lacerated wound right parieto occipital region, Right er bleeding, nasal bleeding,
deformity and abnormal movement of mid and lower 3rd of right leg, left arm, left frontal temporal contusion, comminuted both bone fracture right leg, right parieto occipital and left tempero parietal thin acute SDH, multiple haemorrhagic contusion,
diffuse SAH and tentorial bleed, fracture right Zygoma, comminuted fracture (L)
humerus and fracture right tibia."
13. As per Exhibit X1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the permanent whole body disability of the petitioner was assessed 59.5%.
However, after observing the petitioner and appreciating his oral testimony, the Tribunal, has fixed his functional disability as 75%.
The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent seriously disputed the decision of the Tribunal in fixing the functional disability of the petitioner at 75%.

According to him, the Tribunal was not justified in enhancing the functional disability of the petitioner more than what is assessed by the Medical Board and stated in Exhibit X1.
14.
It is true that as per Exhibit X1, the whole body disability of the petitioner is fixed by the medical board at 59.5%.
According to the petitioner, MACA. No.2173/2015 & CO.22/2021 2025:KER:11455 he is a businessman.
When he was examined as PW1, he deposed that after the incident, he could not do any work.
The petitioner was treated as inpatient for a total period of 40 days.
On a perusal of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it can be seen that in the accident he sustained very serious injuries including five fractures.

It was in the above context, the Tribunal, after observing the petitioner and after evaluating his oral testimony, came to a conclusion that the disability suffered by the petitioner has seriously affected his earning capacity and came to the conclusion that the functional disability will come to 75%.

The reasons given by the Tribunal for arriving at functional disability of the petitioner at 75% are valid, genuine and sustainable and therefore, I do not find any grounds to interfere with the same.
15. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 44 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to MACA. No.2173/2015 & CO.22/2021 2025:KER:11455 Rs.12,60,000/-.
16.

The learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent would argue that the Tribunal's has awarded a sum of Rs.4,41,000 on the head loss of earning power and another Rs.3,50,000/- on the head 'compensation for continuing partial or permanent disability, in addition to Rs.40,000/- on the head 'pain and suffering.
No separate compensation is seen awarded on the head loss of amenities.
Since, towards loss of disability a sum of Rs.12,60,000/- was awarded, separate compensation on the head 'loss of earning power' is to be deducted.

17. Considering the nature of the injuries sustained including five fractures and the fact that he was treated as inpatient for a period of 40 days, I hold that compensation awarded on the head pain and suffering is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.

For the very same reasons,
he is also entitled to get reasonable compensation on the head 'loss of amenities in life', which is also fixed at Rs.1,00,000/-.
18. Towards loss of earning, the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.21,000/- being the income for 6 months @Rs.3500/-.

Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.8,000/-, towards loss of earning he is MACA. No.2173/2015 & CO.22/2021 2025:KER:11455 entitled to get a sum of Rs. 48,000/- (8000x6months).
19.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
20. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.1689600, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
